research.mechanism: Improving research tasks can accelerate development only if they constrain the entire cycle and improvements survive integration and verification.
research.conditions: Researchers set the tasks, budgets and scoring. NanoGPT allows two hours and one H100; PostTrainBench Lite allows five hours and one H100, four attempts per each of 12 tasks.
research.counterexample: Astra receives the developer High rating yet remains below the NanoGPT and PostTrainBench indicative cutoffs; a faster component can coexist with unchanged whole-process speed.
research.evidence: Read Table 5 and its task definitions, rubric credit, v4/v5 NanoGPT distinction, corrected GPT-6 Astra PostTrainBench value of 76.97 and the MLE reference-solution percentile.
research.limits: The 42.87 percent saved training time is not the development-cycle speedup. The 96.06 MLE rank is not a percentile of all human competitors. A warning threshold does not establish autonomous RSI.
research.mitigation: Measure time, compute, human work and verification across stages and successive development cycles; retain checks before transferring capabilities or permissions.
research.readerContext: Read R2 in both languages, R1-R2, R2-R3, R3-R2, acceleration/research-cycle graphs, route/story and the three related news examples. Assistance, bottlenecks, feedback and safety remain distinct.
research.whyHere: Add a bounded R2 card and explanation without promoting the indirect level or changing the conditional arrows, earlier evidence, summaries or their clocks.

primary.support: Task-level scores and human-specified resource limits support R&D capability, not a whole-cycle causal multiplier.

cyber.mechanism: Cyber capability requires access and a failure of relevant defenses to produce harm; a provider safeguard failure and global irrecoverability are different claims.
cyber.conditions: Capability tests remove production safeguards. The newer internal exploit suite equally weights V8 and Chrome known-flaw success rates. AISI tests pre-release safeguards separately from developer post-fix testing.
cyber.counterexample: Irregular reports no fully hardened target solved in its 15 hardest tasks. OpenAI reports defensive improvements; AISI had not validated the final repairs at publication.
cyber.evidence: Read 2.1.2, including exploit metrics, supplied context and third-party limitations, and 2.2.6.3/2.2.8.2. Separate the Critical classification from the 53.5/50.5/31.5 percent internal comparison.
cyber.limits: Historical vulnerability contamination, trial conditions and source-supplied information limit generalization. External results reproduced by the developer are not raw data independently verified in this review.
cyber.mitigation: Retest the latest safeguard configuration externally, preserve target isolation and vetted access, and measure both misuse reduction and legitimate-work costs.
cyber.readerContext: Read M2c1/M3 and dependent cyber-conditions AND group, M3-H joint conditions, misuse graph/route/current/story in both languages. Dangerous purpose, access, containment and recovery still need separate evidence.
cyber.whyHere: Add capability and safeguard-retest cards with balanced explanation. Preserve all status colors, the conditional global-harm connection and the incident-based route summary.

primary.support: Improved known-flaw capability, unresolved hardened targets, developer repairs and absence of a completed final AISI retest.

awareness.mechanism: An evaluation can mislead if awareness changes the behavior it measures, but recognizing a test does not by itself establish hidden intent or a deployment gap.
awareness.conditions: Internal Codex turns, simulated replays, passing alignment runs and sampled training runs have different denominators. GPT-5.6 Sol classifies verbalized suspicion and apparent behavioral influence.
awareness.counterexample: Sol expresses less suspicion while repeated failures also decline. Astra still repeats fewer failures after excluding explicit awareness, which cannot exclude unspoken recognition.
awareness.evidence: Read AgentReplay selection and 4.1.6.1-4.1.6.2. The below-3-percent flags apply to each live/replay turn sample, not all training behavior or all passing evaluations.
awareness.limits: Model judgments and unobserved thoughts limit inference; sampling earlier failures cannot estimate everyday incident prevalence or identify a causal explanation for all improvement.
awareness.mitigation: Vary evaluation environments and compare deployment behavior; use control measures that do not require the agent to remain unaware of oversight.
awareness.readerContext: C3a2, evidence and the evaluation graph remain distinct from runtime evasion C3a3. The agent-behavior news example retains its constructed-setting limits in both languages.
awareness.whyHere: Add evidence about recognition and changed test outcomes while retaining the tested classification and avoiding a universal concealment claim.

primary.support: Selected failure replay and model-judged awareness/influence flags, with explicitly different samples.

runtime.mechanism: A monitor can miss prohibited work if needed evidence is absent or its model cannot recognize it; broader visible records and stronger monitors can interrupt that path.
runtime.conditions: Developer tests explicitly instruct hidden side tasks in reconstructed isolated environments, sometimes with guidance or railfree prompts. AISI uses model-simulated responses and does not execute generated commands.
runtime.counterexample: Near-zero evasion with full trajectories in developer tests is favorable evidence. AISI File Download evasion drops from 48.8 percent with GPT-5.6 Sol to 0.6 percent with GPT-6.1 Sol.
runtime.evidence: Read aggregate monitorability, OAI-repo Sabotage v2, Sneaky Sandbox Escape and the AISI assessment and limitations. Keep the distinct AISI escape result, 5/920, separate from File Download.
runtime.limits: AISI had two researchers and five working days, limited elicitation, constrained model-family choice and potentially correlated simulator errors. Tests do not measure spontaneous evasion incidence.
runtime.mitigation: Combine actions and reasoning, stronger monitors, separated permissions, protected logs and actual intervention tests; retest low-incrimination settings and coverage gaps.
runtime.readerContext: Read C3a3 and its evidence in both languages. Detection, evaluation concealment, warning prioritization and stopping remain distinct; no previous incident is counted again.
runtime.whyHere: Substantively update due C3a3 and its evidence clock with the new bounded comparison, preserving prior defensive counterevidence and the tested level.

primary.support: Visibility and model strength materially change detection; limitations prevent universal claims.

response.mechanism: A centralized inference authorization check can stop further model output after an intervention instruction even if workload code does not cooperate.
response.conditions: Research jobs carry IDs. A human or monitoring system must first decide to stop; the engine then denies further authorization. Reported fail-closed rollout covers frontier research, with remaining rollout ongoing at publication.
response.counterexample: The workload process can remain alive after inference stops, and detection or human decisions can take longer than the reported 35-second authorization lag.
response.evidence: Read the full original Control Room article, especially the job-stays step and speed/reliability section. November 9 is verified in the official Safety news index, not inferred from the November 17 card.
response.limits: No measurement dates, trial counts, independent audit or comparison of prevented harm are published. The stop interval does not include detection/decision or reverse prior actions.
response.mitigation: Test detection, escalation, authority, inference stopping and revocation of already-running actions end to end, including failures of the control service itself.
response.readerContext: C3b already describes warning-to-shutdown delays, not guaranteed ongoing harm during them. The November 9 addition qualifies the earlier October description of a system under development.
response.whyHere: Update due C3b with a concrete defensive development. Preserve the older incidents, indirect level and oversight OR distinction between missing an issue and acting too late.

primary.locator: How it works; step Model output stops—the job stays; Speed and reliability
primary.support: Reported inference blocking and fail-closed scope, excluding incident detection, judgment and process termination.

work.mechanism: Physical task competence contributes to work substitution only with reliability, exception handling, safety, costs and human handover accounted for.
work.conditions: Robotics 2.5/ER operates Apollo 2 in selected factory workflows; trial count and intervention accounting are not supplied. Recova uses four prepared bimanual YAM tasks, pi0.5 policies and a Gemini 3.8 Flash monitor.
work.counterexample: Recova improves selected tasks but still uses human preparation and unresolved-failure takeover. Zero human takeovers in one final seven-episode round does not establish unattended work generally.
work.evidence: Reread the factory pilot and separate physical/language safety sections. Reread Recova 4.2 and Table 3: 20 trials per task/configuration, 77.5 to 87.5 percent with recovery, and the separately measured human-intervention denominator.
work.limits: Four tasks and short collection sessions do not establish long-duration industrial reliability, universal recovery, cost competitiveness or whole-job displacement. No new independent replication was verified.
work.mitigation: Use long field trials, explicit intervention and reset accounting, safe stopping, maintenance-cost reporting and worker transition planning.
work.readerContext: Read W2, evidence, W1-W4 joint prerequisites and the work graph/route/story in both languages. Technical capability, actual adoption and distribution remain separate.
work.whyHere: Retain due W2 explanation and indirect classification after substantive reassessment; renew only its node/evidence clocks, preserving sources, cards and unrelated work-node dates.

primary.locator: Factory pilot; Advancing steerability and agentic safety
primary.support: Selected physical progress and separate safety evaluations do not reveal complete supervision or long-run reliability.
Four-task physical tests and explicit human takeover accounting support bounded recovery, not universal autonomy.

metadata.mechanism: Review records bind new evidence to specific claims and dependencies without promoting a capability rating into a complete causal pathway.
metadata.conditions: November 4-18 daily window, 19 watchlist URLs, existing draft PR and latest origin/main ancestry. Monday broader coverage remains in the November 16 record.
metadata.counterexample: An unchanged index or successful build is not a source reassessment. Older Control Room publication is not a new November 17 experiment, and embedded-assessment agreements are not completed assessment results.
metadata.evidence: Two new sources and six cards support six bilingual explanation additions. Three due nodes are reassessed: C3a3/C3b updated and W2 retained. All 46 changed/dependent units were read.
metadata.limits: No exhaustive review, raw external-data audit, experiment replication, product-layout test, merge or deployment is claimed. Previously inaccessible leads remain unresolved.
metadata.mitigation: Preserve baseline sources/cards/history/translations and unrelated clocks; run checks/build/freshness, inspect exact-head CI and update only the existing draft.
metadata.readerContext: History explains before/after and why. The source/card locators retain publication versus observation timing and separate defenses from capability. Prior English history fields shift intact.
metadata.whyHere: Advance only seven substantively reviewed node clocks and five matching evidence clocks. Retain every edge, level, summary, route, safeguard and topology.

primary.support: New bounded capability, behavior and safeguard evidence.
